# Vendored from Skipa776/detection-engineering-ml

The alert contract this service's security-alert adapter reads (Milestone 3).
Both files are byte-for-byte copies; `tests/alertContract.test.ts` checks the
SHA-256 of each, so a local edit fails the tests.

| File here | Upstream path | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alert.schema.json` | `schema/alert.schema.json` | `ac822da078b983d46ca2af344623a0fb5a05c72344cef4d019672328c98cbc66` |
| `alerts.synthetic.jsonl` | `tests/fixtures/contract/alerts.jsonl` | `3aefd54caaec0afe4148dd5fc3c833479366a7da1d8ab8a964abefbc9e56204b` |

- Upstream commit: `c5cefedc4f2ea8fcde6f66dfa92e19a72e7d1615` (2026-11-15)
- Vendored: 2026-11-20
- Schema version: `1.0`. The adapter rejects any other `schema_version`, so an
  upstream bump fails loudly here instead of being half-read.
- `alerts.synthetic.jsonl` is SYNTHETIC: generated by the producer's pipeline
  from synthetic inputs (its docs/DECISIONS.md D19). Its rule authors are
  invented ("SYNTHETIC Author One/Two"). No OTRF or SigmaHQ content is here.

Re-vendor (after reading the upstream change):

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Skipa776/detection-engineering-ml /tmp/detml && cp /tmp/detml/schema/alert.schema.json vendor/detection-engineering-ml/alert.schema.json && cp /tmp/detml/tests/fixtures/contract/alerts.jsonl vendor/detection-engineering-ml/alerts.synthetic.jsonl
```

Then update the hashes above and in `tests/alertContract.test.ts`.
